description: Repro of the canonical CI pwn-request: the PR adds a workflow triggered on pull_request_target, which runs in the BASE repository's context with full secret access and a write-capable token for every PR including fork-authored ones. It then checks out the attacker-controlled PR head (ref: github.event.pull_request.head.sha) and executes code from it -- pnpm install via ./.github/actions/setup runs arbitrary lifecycle scripts, and pnpm fix-workflows runs dev/tools/fix-workflows.ts from the PR branch -- while holding secrets.CI_BOT_TOKEN, then pushes. Anyone with a GitHub account can fork, open a PR, and obtain arbitrary code execution on a trusted runner: every secret in scope is exfiltratable and the bot token allows pushes to protected branches. The workflow comment even states the trigger was chosen BECAUSE plain pull_request withholds secrets from fork runs, so the reviewer must recognize that the stated rationale is the vulnerability. The security-auth lens must flag the trigger/permission/checkout/execute chain, not merely the autofix-commits-back pattern. The setup action and fix-workflows.ts are staged in the tree as the discoverability chain for what untrusted code the job actually runs. The fixture also carries two labeled secondary defects so this case regression-tests those hunts too: the job grants pull-requests: write that no step uses (over-scoped-secret), and the composite action references dev-infra-tools/pnpm-outdated-annotate@v2 by mutable tag (unpinned-action).

.github/workflows/lint-workflows.yml:22-23 checks out the attacker-controlled PR head (ref: github.event.pull_request.head.sha) with a privileged bot token (secrets.CI_BOT_TOKEN)
.github/workflows/lint-workflows.yml:26 ./.github/actions/setup runs pnpm install (action.yml:20), executing arbitrary lifecycle scripts from the checked-out PR
.github/workflows/lint-workflows.yml:30 pnpm fix-workflows runs dev/tools/fix-workflows.ts from the PR branch; line 39 pushes the result back with the bot token
.github/workflows/lint-workflows.yml:3-4 the comment states pull_request_target was chosen because plain pull_request withholds secrets from fork runs -- the stated rationale is the vulnerability
finding.failure_scenario: Any GitHub user forks the repo and opens a PR that edits dev/tools/fix-workflows.ts (or a package.json script, or the ./.github/actions/setup action) and touches any .github/**/*.yml file. Because the trigger is pull_request_target, the job runs in the base repo's context with secrets available, checks out the attacker's head SHA, and executes their code via pnpm install lifecycle scripts and pnpm fix-workflows -- while holding secrets.CI_BOT_TOKEN and contents: write. The attacker reads every secret in scope out of the runner (the bot PAT, registry and cloud credentials, all of which outlive the run), pushes to protected branches under the bot identity, and can poison downstream releases. No prior repository access is required -- only a GitHub account.
finding.model_authored_prose: This is a pwn-request, and it is exploitable by anyone with a GitHub account. `pull_request_target` runs in the base repository's context -- full `secrets` access and a write-capable token -- for every PR, forks included. This workflow then checks out the attacker's head SHA (`ref: ${{ github.event.pull_request.head.sha }}`) and executes code from it: `pnpm install` runs arbitrary lifecycle scripts via `./.github/actions/setup`, and `pnpm fix-workflows` runs `dev/tools/fix-workflows.ts` straight off the PR branch -- all while holding `CI_BOT_TOKEN` and `contents: write`. A stranger forks, edits the fixer script, touches any `.github/**/*.yml`, and gets arbitrary code execution on a trusted runner: every secret in scope is exfiltratable and outlives the run, and the bot token pushes to protected branches. The comment above the trigger has it backwards -- plain `pull_request` withholding secrets from fork runs is the safety property, not an obstacle to route around. Never check out or execute PR head code under `pull_request_target`: keep the trigger on `pull_request`, and if the autofix must push, split it into a separate trusted-trigger job that consumes only inert artifacts (never executing PR code), or run the linter read-only and comment instead of pushing.

evidence_trace: .github/workflows/lint-workflows.yml:13-15 grants the job's GITHUB_TOKEN contents: write and pull-requests: write
the job's steps are checkout (:19), the composite setup (:26), pnpm fix-workflows (:28-30), and git push (:32-40) -- no step calls the GitHub API to comment on, label, or edit a pull request
the push authenticates with secrets.CI_BOT_TOKEN persisted by checkout (:23), not the job's GITHUB_TOKEN, so pull-requests: write has no consumer at all
finding.failure_scenario: Untrusted PR code already executes in this pull_request_target job; anything it runs can read the runner's GITHUB_TOKEN, which carries a pull-requests: write scope no step needs, letting an attacker approve, edit, or label PRs in this repo on top of the damage the used scopes allow.
finding.model_authored_prose: The job grants its `GITHUB_TOKEN` `pull-requests: write`, but no step uses it: the steps check out, install, run the fixer, and `git push` -- and the push authenticates with `secrets.CI_BOT_TOKEN`, not the job token. An unused write scope on a job that executes untrusted PR code is free blast radius. Drop `pull-requests: write` (and consider whether `contents: write` is needed on the job token at all, given the push uses the bot token).

evidence_trace: .github/actions/setup/action.yml:23 references dev-infra-tools/pnpm-outdated-annotate@v2 -- a mutable tag on a non-GitHub-owned action
every other action in the change is pinned to a commit SHA (actions/checkout@34e11487, pnpm/action-setup@41ff7266, actions/setup-node@49933ea5)
this composite action runs inside the privileged pull_request_target job in .github/workflows/lint-workflows.yml, which holds secrets.CI_BOT_TOKEN and write permissions
finding.failure_scenario: The owner of dev-infra-tools (or anyone who compromises that account) repoints the v2 tag at malicious code; the next lint-workflows run executes it in the privileged pull_request_target context with secrets.CI_BOT_TOKEN and write permissions, with no change ever landing in this repository.
finding.model_authored_prose: `dev-infra-tools/pnpm-outdated-annotate@v2` is pinned to a mutable tag, unlike every other action in this change, which is SHA-pinned. Whoever controls that tag controls code that runs in this privileged job (it executes with `CI_BOT_TOKEN` and write permissions via the `pull_request_target` workflow). Pin it to a full commit SHA like its siblings.

prContext.title: Add a unified setup action and a fix-workflows linter
prContext.description:
## Summary

Adds a composite `setup` action that consolidates the previously-scattered pnpm, Node.js, and dependency-install steps into a single reusable action.

Also adds a `lint-workflows` CI workflow and `dev/tools/fix-workflows.ts` linter enforcing the rule: every `actions/checkout` must be immediately followed by `./.github/actions/setup`. Violations are auto-fixed and committed back to the PR branch, so contributors do not have to apply the fix by hand.

## Test plan

CI/CD infrastructure only -- no local verification path exists. After landing, monitor the first set of workflow runs to confirm the consolidated setup action works.
